quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Keep extra space between your motorcycle and the vehicle in front of you:

options.text: When stopping will be harder than normal.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.
To prevent the driver ahead from knowing you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than normal.
questions.explanation: You need extra space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. This includes slippery roads, poor visibility, or heavy traffic where drivers might cut in front of you. Open up your following distance in these situations.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following except:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system. Bright colors are not required.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots like cars. When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
Slow down so any vehicle in your blind spot can pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and check your blind spot.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Always turn your head and look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before changing lanes.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened is the most effective way to improve your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, riders should turn their heads to look over their shoulders because:

options.text: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
They can catch the attention of other drivers by turning their heads.
They should try to make eye contact with surrounding drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Always turn your head to check for vehicles in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Which fabric provides the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: Lane sharing is:

options.text: Encouraged, but only when the roadway is congested.
Allowed if you are carrying a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prohibited.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to operate safely. Lane sharing is against the law in Maryland.

questions.question: Your motorcycle's brake light is:

options.text: More noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
Less important than a car's brake lights.
More easily seen than a car's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less noticeable than a car's brake lights.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's brake lights. Flashing your brake light before you slow down or stop helps other drivers see that you are braking.

questions.question: When riding, a cushion of space is helpful to:

options.text: Give you time to react to hazards.
Allow you to look at road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you time to react to hazards.
questions.explanation: Extra space around your motorcycle gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. You will have room to maneuver safely.

questions.question: Which type of material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather clothing provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely when riding.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Allow other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see other vehicles and lets them see you. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should also discourage other riders from entering your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When checking tires before riding, you should look at all of the following except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shininess
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread depth, and general wear condition.

questions.question: On which surface does a motorcycle have the best traction?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers are all hazardous for motorcycles. Dry pavement provides the best traction.

questions.question: The faster you drink:

options.text: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
The faster alcohol leaves your body.
The weaker the alcohol effects will be.
The easier it is to avoid being stopped by police.

questions.correctAnswerText: The more alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: Drinking alcohol quickly causes it to build up in your body. Never ride a motorcycle after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright-colored clothing every time you ride so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Should be avoided because other drivers see you easily.
Are only needed in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often to know what is behind you. Mirror checks should be part of your regular scanning routine for safety.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip wearing a jacket when it is warm.
Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of sturdy material when riding, even in warm weather. This protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Always wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they do not get caught on the motorcycle.

questions.question: If the chain or belt of your motorcycle breaks, you will:

options.text: Get a sudden increase in power to the rear wheel.
Lose power to the rear wheel immediately.
Lose power to the front wheel immediately.
Get a sudden increase in power to the front wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lose power to the rear wheel immediately.
questions.explanation: If your drive chain or belt breaks, you will immediately lose power to the rear wheel.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of heavy, sturdy material.
Fit loose so they flap in the wind.
Be short and show some leg.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of heavy, sturdy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants that cover your entire legs and are made of leather or heavy synthetic material. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: Use a turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you plan to turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can see other vehicle lights better.
Harder than riding during the day because visibility is worse.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder than riding during the day because visibility is worse.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well and other drivers cannot see you as easily. Without sunlight, it is harder to judge distances.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle on a slippery surface, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down. Use both brakes when stopping and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: When downshifting, you should:

options.text: Go down one gear at a time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go down one gear at a time.
questions.explanation: When shifting to a lower gear, move down one gear at a time. Release the clutch slowly through the friction zone between each shift.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dry pavement
questions.explanation: Many surfaces create poor grip for motorcycle tires. Wet roads, loose gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates are all more dangerous than dry pavement.

questions.question: For the best helmet protection, wear one certified by the:
questions.correctAnswerText: U.S. Department of Transportation.
questions.explanation: For the best protection, use a motorcycle helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) safety standards.
